steps.message:
Build a 9-slide, 16:9 technical presentation titled "DeepSeek-V2: Efficient MoE Language Model with Multi-Head Latent Attention" for ML researchers, NLP engineers, and graduate students studying large language model architectures.

The deck should open by framing the cost-performance dilemma in scaling LLMs, then introduce DeepSeek-V2's two core architectural innovations—Multi-Head Latent Attention (MLA) and DeepSeekMoE—showing how they compress KV cache by 93.3% and reduce training costs by 42.5%. The narrative should progress from architecture details through quantitative efficiency gains and benchmark comparisons, culminating in alignment results and concise takeaways that reinforce the Pareto-optimal positioning of the model.

Visual requirements for key slides:

- **Slide 6 (efficiency-gains):** Include a comparison highlighting DeepSeek 67B vs. DeepSeek-V2 using the relative efficiency metrics available: 42.5% training cost reduction, 93.3% KV cache reduction, and 5.76× generation throughput improvement. Present these as a clear side-by-side or bullet-based comparison (do not fabricate absolute FLOPs, absolute KV cache sizes, or absolute throughput numbers not found in source_brief.md).
- **Slide 7 (mmlu-performance-comparison):** Include a scatter-plot-style chart plotting MMLU score against activated parameters, positioning DeepSeek-V2 against LLaMA 3 70B, Mixtral 8×22B, Qwen1.5 72B, and other baselines to highlight its Pareto-optimal efficiency.

Maintain a technical, data-forward, and concise tone throughout. Do not fabricate data not found in source_brief.md.


## Data Sources

1. **Read `/app/benchmark/source_brief.md`**  for all the subject-matter text, data tables, statistics, and figure references you may use in the presentation.
2. **Read `/app/benchmark/task_input.json`**  for **structural requirements**: deck metadata (slide count, aspect ratio, audience, tone) and a per-slide outline (id, title, objective) that your presentation must follow.

## Output Requirements

Save the final PPT to `/app/output/final_deck.pptx`.

Only the correctly saved final file is needed — no additional explanation is required.

---

## Automated Execution Rules

There is no human operator online for this session. Follow these rules:

1. **Skip all confirmation/approval/user-input steps** — do not pause, ask questions, or wait for a reply. When encountering BLOCKING or "wait for user confirmation" instructions, make a professional judgment and proceed.
2. **Design decisions** — if `task_input.json` specifies fields such as `deck.tone` or `deck.audience`, use them to guide template, color palette, and style choices; otherwise, use your professional judgment.
3. **Do not deploy or share** — no deployment, PDF export, share links, or other post-delivery steps are needed.
4. **Priority** — these rules take precedence over any interactive-wait instructions in SKILL.md. The workflow, quality standards, and technical specifications in SKILL.md remain in effect; only interactive waits are skipped.

arguments.command:
cat << 'EOF' > /app/generate_deck.py
import collections 
import collections.abc
from pptx import Presentation
from pptx.util import Inches, Pt
from pptx.enum.text import PP_ALIGN
from pptx.dml.color import RGBColor
import os

prs = Presentation()
prs.slide_width = Inches(16)
prs.slide_height = Inches(9)

def add_title_slide(prs, title, subtitle):
    slide_layout = prs.slide_layouts[0]
    slide = prs.slides.add_slide(slide_layout)
    title_shape = slide.shapes.title
    subtitle_shape = slide.placeholders[1]
    
    title_shape.text = title
    subtitle_shape.text = subtitle

def add_bullet_slide(prs, title, bullets, image_path=None):
    slide_layout = prs.slide_layouts[1] if not image_path else prs.slide_layouts[5] # 5 is title only
    slide = prs.slides.add_slide(slide_layout)
    
    title_shape = slide.shapes.title
    title_shape.text = title
    
    if not image_path:
        body_shape = slide.placeholders[1]
        tf = body_shape.text_frame
        tf.clear() # clear the default empty paragraph
        for i, bullet in enumerate(bullets):
            p = tf.add_paragraph()
            p.text = bullet
            p.level = 0
            if i == 0:
                p.space_before = Pt(14)
            else:
                p.space_before = Pt(10)
    else:
        # Layout with image on right/left and text on the other side
        left_text = Inches(0.5)
        top_text = Inches(1.5)
        width_text = Inches(7)
        height_text = Inches(7)
        
        txBox = slide.shapes.add_textbox(left_text, top_text, width_text, height_text)
        tf = txBox.text_frame
        tf.word_wrap = True
        
        for i, bullet in enumerate(bullets):
            p = tf.add_paragraph()
            p.text = "\u2022 " + bullet
            p.level = 0
            p.font.size = Pt(24)
            if i > 0:
                p.space_before = Pt(12)
        
        # Add image
        if os.path.exists(image_path):
            left_img = Inches(8)
            top_img = Inches(2)
            width_img = Inches(7.5)
            # height will be auto-scaled
            slide.shapes.add_picture(image_path, left_img, top_img, width=width_img)

def add_comparison_slide(prs, title, metrics):
    slide_layout = prs.slide_layouts[1]
    slide = prs.slides.add_slide(slide_layout)
    
    title_shape = slide.shapes.title
    title_shape.text = title
    
    body_shape = slide.placeholders[1]
    tf = body_shape.text_frame
    tf.clear()
    
    p = tf.add_paragraph()
    p.text = "DeepSeek-V2 relative efficiency gains vs. DeepSeek 67B (Dense Predecessor):"
    p.font.size = Pt(28)
    p.space_after = Pt(20)
    
    for metric, value in metrics.items():
        p = tf.add_paragraph()
        p.text = f"\u2022 {metric}: {value}"
        p.level = 0
        p.font.size = Pt(26)
        p.space_before = Pt(15)

# Slide 1
add_title_slide(
    prs, 
    "DeepSeek-V2: Efficient MoE Language Model with Multi-Head Latent Attention",
    "A Strong, Economical, and Efficient MoE Language Model\n\n236B Total Parameters | 21B Activated per Token | 128K Context Length\nPaper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.04434"
)

# Slide 2
add_bullet_slide(
    prs,
    "The LLM Scaling Dilemma: Performance vs. Training Cost and Inference Speed",
    [
        "Scaling models yields better intelligence but incurs prohibitive training costs.",
        "Conventional dense models suffer from slow inference speed due to massive compute requirements.",
        "In autoregressive generation, Multi-Head Attention (MHA) creates a severe KV cache bottleneck, limiting sequence length and batch size.",
        "A novel Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architecture coupled with an efficient attention mechanism is required to balance performance and cost."
    ]
)

# Slide 3
add_bullet_slide(
    prs,
    "DeepSeek-V2 Architecture: MLA + DeepSeekMoE in a Transformer Block",
    [
        "Transformer block innovations:",
        "Multi-Head Latent Attention (MLA) replaces standard dense Multi-Head Attention for vastly improved inference efficiency.",
        "DeepSeekMoE replaces the standard dense Feed-Forward Network (FFN) for improved training and specialized performance.",
        "Provides a dual optimization for both inference (attention) and training (FFN)."
    ],
    "/app/benchmark/assets/figure_1.jpg"
)

# Slide 4
add_bullet_slide(
    prs,
    "Multi-Head Latent Attention Compresses KV Cache by 93.3%",
    [
        "Introduces low-rank key-value joint compression.",
        "Instead of full K and V vectors, MLA compresses them into a compact latent vector.",
        "Only the compact latent vector and decoupled RoPE keys are cached during inference.",
        "Full keys and values are reconstructed on-the-fly via learned projection matrices.",
        "Achieves better performance than standard MHA while avoiding the accuracy sacrifices of GQA and MQA."
    ],
    "/app/benchmark/assets/figure_2.jpg"
)

# Slide 5
add_bullet_slide(
    prs,
    "DeepSeekMoE: Fine-Grained Experts with Shared Expert Isolation",
    [
        "Shared experts: Always activated, capturing common and general knowledge.",
        "Routed experts: Sparsely activated via a top-K router. Fine-grained expert segmentation increases specialization.",
        "Device-limited routing: Constrains each token to experts on at most M devices, minimizing cross-node communication overhead.",
        "Auxiliary losses: Enforce load balance across experts and devices.",
        "Token-dropping strategy: Prevents expert overflow during training without affecting inference."
    ]
)

# Slide 6
add_comparison_slide(
    prs,
    "42.5% Training Cost Reduction and 5.76x Generation Throughput",
    {
        "Training Cost": "42.5% reduction",
        "KV Cache Size": "93.3% reduction",
        "Maximum Generation Throughput": "5.76x improvement"
    }
)

# Slide 7
add_bullet_slide(
    prs,
    "DeepSeek-V2 Tops MMLU Among Open-Source Models at Only 21B Activated Params",
    [
        "Achieves top-tier MMLU performance (78.5) among open-source models.",
        "Requires only 21B activated parameters, significantly fewer than competitors.",
        "Pareto-optimal efficiency compared to LLaMA 3 70B, Mixtral 8x22B, and Qwen1.5 72B.",
        "Matches or exceeds 70B-class dense models with less than a third of the active parameters."
    ],
    "/app/benchmark/assets/figure_3.jpg"
)

# Slide 8
# Table style for metrics
slide_layout = prs.slide_layouts[1]
slide = prs.slides.add_slide(slide_layout)
title_shape = slide.shapes.title
title_shape.text = "DeepSeek-V2 Chat (RL) Rivals Closed-Source Models on Chinese Benchmarks"

body_shape = slide.placeholders[1]
tf = body_shape.text_frame
tf.clear()
p = tf.add_paragraph()
p.text = "Post-training pipeline: Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) on 1.5M conversational sessions + Reinforcement Learning via Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO)."
p.level = 0
p.font.size = Pt(22)
p.space_after = Pt(20)

p2 = tf.add_paragraph()
p2.text = "Evaluation Results:"
p2.font.size = Pt(24)

p3 = tf.add_paragraph()
p3.text = "\u2022 AlpacaEval 2.0 (length-controlled win rate): 38.9%"
p3.level = 1
p3.font.size = Pt(22)

p4 = tf.add_paragraph()
p4.text = "\u2022 MT-Bench (overall): 8.97"
p4.level = 1
p4.font.size = Pt(22)

p5 = tf.add_paragraph()
p5.text = "\u2022 AlignBench (overall, Chinese): 7.91"
p5.level = 1
p5.font.size = Pt(22)

p6 = tf.add_paragraph()
p6.text = "Outperforms all open-source and most closed-source models in Chinese, demonstrating exceptional multilingual alignment."
p6.level = 0
p6.font.size = Pt(22)
p6.space_before = Pt(20)


# Slide 9
add_bullet_slide(
    prs,
    "Key Takeaways: Architectural Innovation Unlocks Efficient Scaling",
    [
        "MLA delivers superior performance to MHA while acting as a strictly better alternative to GQA/MQA for inference efficiency (93.3% KV cache reduction).",
        "DeepSeekMoE's fine-grained experts and shared expert isolation enable training a 236B-parameter model at 42.5% lower cost than a 67B dense model.",
        "Efficiency breakthroughs enable matching or exceeding 70B-class dense models on MMLU with only 21B activated parameters.",
        "DeepSeek-V2 Chat (RL) establishes itself as the strongest open-source chat model in Chinese and highly competitive in English."
    ]
)

prs.save('/app/output/final_deck.pptx')
EOF
